available: Vercel deployment status and runtime logs
Bounded operational error codes without serialising exception objects or secrets
monitoring.limitation: The public health endpoint proves process reachability only; it does not certify database or provider availability.

rate_limits.discovery: 30 requests per minute per provider-derived client key and server instance
rate_limits.writes: 60 requests per minute per provider-derived client key and server instance
rate_limits.reads: 180 requests per minute per provider-derived client key and server instance
rate_limits.customer_feedback: 30 attempts per 15 minutes per application instance
rate_limits.dish_events: 120 attempts per minute per application instance
rate_limits.verified_behavior: Limits expire, return 429 and Retry-After where implemented; Razorpay webhook bypasses visitor throttling but retains signature verification.
rate_limits.limitation: Counters are in memory and are not a distributed global cap across Vercel instances. A shared edge or durable limiter remains required before higher-risk scale.

retention.current: Browser-saved preferences remain until removed locally. Business submissions, feedback and aggregate dish/day events have no automatic expiry. Temporary in-memory abuse counters expire after one or fifteen minutes depending on the route.
retention.action_taken: No production records were deleted and no retention schedule was invented.
blocked_on: Founder-approved retention periods by record category
Legal operator and privacy policy decisions
Authorised database migration and scheduled-job mechanism

backup_and_recovery.code_rollback: GitHub main commit and Vercel deployment IDs provide a recoverable code history; rollback must target the intended suggest-dish project and then be production-verified.
backup_and_recovery.database: Neon backup/PITR configuration and retention were not accessible or verified. No restore drill was performed.
safe_recovery_sequence: Pause write-heavy or payment workflows if data integrity is uncertain.
Record incident time, affected endpoint and last known healthy deployment without copying secrets into tickets or logs.
Rollback application code only when the failure is code-related; verify /api/health and one read-only recommendation.

For database recovery, identify the intended Neon project and branch, confirm backup/PITR coverage, restore to a separate branch first, compare critical counts and constraints, then obtain founder approval before any production cutover.
Never overwrite or reset the production database as a test.

code_change: Server monitoring logs now emit a bounded error code instead of full exception objects; diagnostic API-key-presence logging was removed.
blockers: No verified automated uptime/error alert and no assigned incident owner.
No approved retention periods or automated deletion mechanism.
No evidence of the intended Neon backup/PITR configuration or a successful isolated restore drill.
Rate limits are per-instance rather than globally distributed.
